native_result.query: In which century did summed social capital peak, what individual social capital components like gold, monument etc increase?
native_result.HypoA: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monuments Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneuosly while summer social capital peaks?
native_result.HypoB: Summed social capital (ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument) peaked in the 14th century BCE (BCE 1400-1301; CE -1400..-1301), within the 2nd millennium BCE / Old Bronze Age (summed Z = 4.24). The components that increase toward/at that peak are Copper & Gold (Z = 2.85 max at BCE 1200-1100; positive significant slope +0.039/century and Spearman rho +0.61) and Monument Count in its later phase (second peak Z = 1.71 at BCE 1400-1300, late mean 0.13 > early mean -0.69, rho +0.43), whereas Amber does not increase (early peak Z = 1.54 in the 4th millennium BCE, then steady decline, slope -0.048/century, rho -0.43).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Parsed capital.csv (BCE axis, comma-decimal handling) and time_series_data.csv (yearly CE axis). 2) Aggregate: summed Z = ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument per century; located max (4.238 @ BCE 1400 & 1300); resolved the tie via century-bin means of the interpolated yearly sum (CopperGold_inter + Amber_inter + MonumentCount_inter) -> 14th century BCE (CE -1400..-1301). 3) Per-component: for each component computed peak value & century (capital + interpolated), full-span OLS slope and Spearman rho over time, early-window (BCE>=3300) vs late-window (BCE<=2000) means, and applied an explicit increase criterion (slope>0 & rho>0 & late_mean>early_mean) plus peak-in-later-half and strong-late-rise checks. 4) Cross-checked interpolated vs capital values at 37 overlapping anchors (max diff 0.0); documented the BCE 4300/4200 coverage gap; kept pollen (Belau/Woserin) documentation-only. 5) Assembled the natural-language hypothesis separating aggregate vs per-component results.

sub_hypo.text: Copper & Gold increases toward/at the summed social-capital peak, with a positive significant slope of +0.039 per century, Spearman rho +0.61, and a component maximum of Z = 2.85 at BCE 1200–1100.

sub_hypo.relations: Copper & Gold increases over advancing time: significant OLS slope +0.039 per century and Spearman rho +0.61. The workflow's increase criterion requires positive slope, positive rho, and a late mean exceeding the early mean; its maximum occurs at BCE 1200–1100.

sub_hypo.text: Monument Count increases in its later phase, with a second peak of Z = 1.71 at BCE 1400–1300, a late mean of 0.13 exceeding an early mean of -0.69, and Spearman rho +0.43.
sub_hypo.context: The later phase of archaeological Monument Count relative to the 14th-century BCE summed social-capital peak; early window BCE ≥3300 versus late window BCE ≤2000.
sub_hypo.relations: Monument Count exhibits a later-phase increase and a second peak at BCE 1400–1300, near the aggregate peak. Its late mean exceeds its early mean (0.13 > -0.69), and its association with advancing time is positive (rho +0.43).

sub_hypo.text: Amber does not increase toward the summed social-capital peak: it peaks early at Z = 1.54 in the 4th millennium BCE and subsequently declines steadily, with slope -0.048 per century and Spearman rho -0.43.
sub_hypo.context: Amber across the archaeological time span, from its 4th-millennium BCE peak toward the later 14th-century BCE aggregate peak.
sub_hypo.relations: Amber declines over advancing time after its early peak, with OLS slope -0.048 per century and Spearman rho -0.43, rather than increasing toward the aggregate peak.
